About MindReader

Think of a famous real person or a fictional character. MindReader asks yes/no questions and, after each answer, updates how likely every character is. It picks the question that is expected to narrow the field the most, and guesses when one character is very likely. One wrong answer lowers the right character's score but never rules it out.

Where the data comes from

Characters and facts come from Wikidata, which is published under CC0. Popularity uses the number of Wikipedia articles about each character. Photos come from Wikimedia Commons and are only shown when their licence allows reuse; the author and licence are shown under every photo. Fictional characters are shown with a generated card, never with copyrighted artwork.

Learning

When you confirm a guess, or tell MindReader who you were thinking of, your answers help it guess better next time. New characters are reviewed by a moderator before they can be guessed.

Privacy

No account, no ads, no tracking cookies. To measure how well the game works, it stores each finished game's answers, the number of questions, the country (from the connection, country level only) and a rough device class. Your browser keeps a random id so repeated games from one device can be weighted fairly; the server only stores a keyed hash of it. Your IP address is used for rate limiting and is not stored.

Images and complaints

If an image or a character entry is wrong or should not be here, use the report form.
